## Paper

The Pure Theory of Public Expenditure

## World

public_goods

## Institution

No-institution public goods baseline.

## Agent type

Contributors/extractors or public-good participants.

## Theoretical benchmark

Private free-riding versus social-optimum contribution/provision brackets.

## Learning setup

Repeated contribution/extraction decisions with a public pool and learned policies.

## Metrics

Contribution rate, extraction rate, welfare, sustainability, collapse indicators.

## Main result

The paper establishes that private and social incentives diverge in public goods provision, leading to underprovision without intervention.

## What they prove

Do not cite this extracted card for a detailed proof without checking the original pages. In this repo, the source is used for the public-goods benchmark idea that private and social incentives can diverge.

## What they only simulate

Not applicable for this card's thesis use: it is a public-economics theory anchor, not a simulation benchmark.

## What they do NOT test

Learning agents, dynamic pool regeneration, extraction rationing, reward-shaping institutions, and multi-seed artificial public-goods runs.

## What we need to reproduce

Report free-rider and social-optimum brackets and show whether learned agents underprovide contributions.

## How our project differs

The theory paper is classical public economics. The repo implements a dynamic commons/public-goods environment with learning agents and institutions.

## Implementation obligations

Free-rider bracket; social optimum bracket; contribution/extraction accounting; pool sustainability; final-window summaries.

## Metrics to compare in our repo

worlds/public_goods/benchmarks.py; outputs/public_goods_full/summary_aggregate.csv.

## Failure modes to audit

Reward-only welfare without state sustainability; no free-rider reference; no contribution metric; treating low sustainability as unexplained noise.

## Project code comparison

Compare The Pure Theory of Public Expenditure to Public Goods benchmarks and full outputs. Baseline low contribution/sustainability should be interpreted against free-rider theory.
